## What I refactored

**`core/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/convert/LenientObjectToEnumConverterFactory.java`** — the `ALIASES` constant.

It used a `LinkedMultiValueMap` builder, a `static {}` block, and a `Collections.unmodifiableMap(...)` wrapper just to hold two fixed entries — and the multi-value capability was never exercised (each key maps to a single value). Collapsed all of that into one immutable literal:

```java
private static final Map<String, List<String>> ALIASES = Map.of("true", List.of("on"), "false", List.of("off"));
```

That's 8 lines → 1, and it lets me drop two now-unused imports (`MultiValueMap`, `LinkedMultiValueMap`) — i.e. removing an abstraction the class didn't actually need.

**Behavior preservation:** the only consumer is `ALIASES.getOrDefault(name, Collections.emptyList())`, a pure lookup with no iteration, so ordering is irrelevant and `Map.of` is exactly equivalent. I verified against `LenientStringToEnumConverterFactoryTests` (`convertFromStringToEnumWhenYamlBooleanShouldConvertValue`), which pins `"true"→ON` and `"false"→OFF`. I also confirmed the remaining imports (`Collections`, `EnumSet`, `List`, `Map`, `Set`) are all still used.
